monthly_review.summary: You've increased volume and intensity this month, with faster paces and higher HR across more demanding sessions — but at the cost of reduced time in foundational aerobic zones (Z1/Z2) and slightly elevated ground contact time.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone distribution shifted sharply: Z1+Z2 dropped from 79% to 54%, while Z3 increased from 19% to 29% — indicating a meaningful shift toward threshold work, likely driving pace gains but potentially compromising recovery and aerobic base durability.

goal_tracker.message: You’ve already exceeded last month’s distance by 5.5 km and need only 1 more run to match last month’s session count — aim for a 5–6 km Zone 2 run before month-end to reinforce aerobic foundation without adding fatigue.

insights.title: Efficiency gain despite higher HR and pace
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency improved from 13.42 to 13.62 (+0.20) even as avg pace quickened and avg HR rose — suggesting better neuromuscular coordination or stride optimization, particularly evident in recent 11 km runs (stride length ~69 cm, ground contact ~314 ms).

insights.title: Sharp reduction in easy-zone volume
insights.body: Time in Z1+Z2 fell from 79% (May) to 54% (June), while Z3 rose from 19% to 29% — meaning nearly half your running time this month was spent at or above lactate threshold, which may limit recovery capacity given only 9 runs vs 10 last month.

insights.title: Cadence-speed dissociation in fast efforts
insights.body: On your fastest recent run (2026-06-11, 6:32 min/km), cadence spiked to 162 spm — yet stride length jumped to 91.13 cm (vs ~69 cm on long runs), indicating efficient power application; however, vertical oscillation also rose to 8.4 cm (+0.7 cm vs long runs), suggesting increased bounce that could elevate injury risk if repeated frequently.

insights.title: High-aerobic-TE short runs offset by low-TE recovery run
insights.body: Three of your five recent runs had aerobic TE ≥3.1 (including two 11 km efforts), but the 3.2 km run on 2026-06-19 had only TE 1.6 at 10:50 min/km and 112 bpm — a true recovery stimulus, though its low volume (3.2 km) may be insufficient to fully offset the preceding load.

recommendations.action: Do a 6.0 km Zone 2 run (HR 128–135 bpm) at ≤9:30 min/km within the next 3 days, focusing on cadence ≥150 spm and ground contact <320 ms.
recommendations.reason: This rebalances zone distribution (currently only 25% Z1/Z2 this month) and supports aerobic recovery after four high-TE runs in the last 15 days.

recommendations.action: In your next 10+ km run, target stride length between 68–70 cm and vertical oscillation ≤7.6 cm — use real-time Garmin metrics to cue form adjustments every 2 km.
recommendations.reason: Your longest runs show consistent stride length (~69.5 cm) and low vertical oscillation (7.7 cm), but the fast 3 km run showed a 0.7 cm increase — reinforcing stability at endurance pace helps efficiency transfer to faster efforts.

recommendations.action: Add 2 × 30-second strides (90–95% max HR) after your next easy run, walking 90 seconds between each.
recommendations.reason: Cadence improved +5 spm this month but remains anchored below 155 spm in most efforts — strides train neuromuscular turnover without elevating overall training stress.

weekly_focus.description: Reinforce Zone 2 durability and form consistency to support continued pace gains while protecting recovery capacity — especially critical given the recent drop in Z1/Z2 time and rising average HR.
suggested_sessions: 8 km mixed terrain run focusing on ground contact <320 ms
